title: Restriction-form finite counit square and quotient targets
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $a:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ be separated and of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and fix one compactification $a=pj$. Write $F_n=Rp_{*,n}j_!$ for compact support on ordinary small pro-etale module derived categories [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support].

Write $G_n=Ra_n^!$ for the finite constructible comparison-class exceptional functor [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], $\omega_n=G_n(A_n)_s$, and $\varepsilon_n:F_n\omega_n\to(A_n)_s$ for its counit. For $m\ge n\ge1$, set $T_W=-\otimes^L_{(A_m)_W}(A_n)_W$, let $\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}$ be scalar restriction, and let $\eta$ be the unit of $T_s\dashv\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}$ [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. Use the specified finite pro-etale realizations of the counit-defined comparison and compact-support coefficient isomorphism [lem-coef-finite-dualizing]:
$$u_{m,n}:T_X\omega_m\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_n,\qquad c_{m,n}:T_sF_m\omega_m\xrightarrow{\sim}F_nT_X\omega_m.$$
Define the morphisms in $D(s_{\mathrm{proet}},A_m)$
$$d_{m,n}=\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}\bigl(F_n(u_{m,n})\circ c_{m,n}\bigr)\circ\eta_{F_m\omega_m},$$
$$v_{m,n}=\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}(\lambda_{m,n})\circ\eta_{(A_m)_s},$$
where $\lambda_{m,n}:T_s(A_m)_s\xrightarrow{\sim}(A_n)_s$ is the canonical scalar-unit isomorphism. Then
$$\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}(\varepsilon_n)\circ d_{m,n}=v_{m,n}\circ\varepsilon_m.$$
Use derived point sections and constant-$R$ restriction [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. There are canonical target isomorphisms
$$\iota_n:\operatorname{Res}^{A_n}_R R\Gamma(s,(A_n)_s)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_n[0],$$
given by the regular coefficient module and its constant sections, under which $R\Gamma(s,v_{m,n})$ is the actual $R$-linear quotient $q_{m,n}[0]:A_m[0]\to A_n[0]$. Thus, with $C_n=\operatorname{Res}^{A_n}_R R\Gamma(s,F_n\omega_n)$, $\bar d_{m,n}=R\Gamma(s,d_{m,n})$ and $e_n=\iota_n\circ R\Gamma(s,\varepsilon_n)$, one has
$$e_n\circ\bar d_{m,n}=q_{m,n}[0]\circ e_m\quad\text{in }D(R).$$
The sheaf-level and section-level assertions include $m=n$ and agree with successive quotient compositions. They involve only the finite exceptional counits, the chosen compactification and scalar adjunctions; no strict dualizing representative or test object is chosen.

proof.text: Put $b_{m,n}=F_n(u_{m,n})\circ c_{m,n}$. Apply [lem-coef-finite-dualizing] with its $A=A_m$, $B=A_n$. Its counit identity, including the canonical scalar-unit identification $\lambda_{m,n}$, gives $\varepsilon_n\circ F_n(u_{m,n})=\lambda_{m,n}\circ T_s(\varepsilon_m)\circ c_{m,n}^{-1}$. Compose on the right with $c_{m,n}$ to obtain $\varepsilon_n\circ b_{m,n}=\lambda_{m,n}\circ T_s(\varepsilon_m)$. The same node specifies the finite pro-etale realization, so this is an equality for the counits and the chosen compact-support comparisons in the statement, without assuming an exceptional adjoint on arbitrary pro-etale inputs.

proof.text: Write $\operatorname{Res}=\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}$ and $\eta=\eta^{m,n}$. The tensor-restriction adjunction of [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower] has natural unit, so $\operatorname{Res}(T_s\varepsilon_m)\circ\eta_{F_m\omega_m}=\eta_{(A_m)_s}\circ\varepsilon_m$. Functoriality of restriction and step 1 therefore give the explicit calculation $$\operatorname{Res}(\varepsilon_n)\circ d_{m,n}=\operatorname{Res}(\varepsilon_n\circ b_{m,n})\circ\eta_{F_m\omega_m}=\operatorname{Res}(\lambda_{m,n})\circ\operatorname{Res}(T_s\varepsilon_m)\circ\eta_{F_m\omega_m}=v_{m,n}\circ\varepsilon_m.$$ Only naturality of the unit and associativity of composition are used here.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pod-point-exact-extension-sections] at the finite pair $(A_n,(A_n)_s)$. Its exact sections functor computes derived sections termwise, and its constant-value ring isomorphism $A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(s,(A_n)_s)$ identifies the regular module with its constant sections. The inverse, placed in degree zero and restricted along $R\to A_n$, is precisely $\iota_n$. This uses the finite constant coefficient sheaf, not the completed integral sheaf, and gives an isomorphism of objects of $D(R)$, rather than just a cohomology-group identification.

source.place: Second paragraph, final sentences: comparisons defined by their counits identify the specified natural maps; expanded restriction-form calculation.

proof.text: Compute $v_{m,n}$ on the regular sheaf $(A_m)_s$ itself. It is free of rank one over itself and concentrated in degree zero, so its tensor with $(A_n)_s$ already computes the derived tensor. The unit formula in [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower] sends a local section $a$ to $a\otimes1$, and $\lambda_{m,n}$ sends $a\otimes b$ to $q_{m,n}(a)b$. Hence $v_{m,n}$ is exactly the constant-sheaf quotient map $a\mapsto q_{m,n}(a)$. Evaluating on constant sections with the identifications of step 3 gives $$\iota_n\circ R\Gamma(s,v_{m,n})=q_{m,n}[0]\circ\iota_m,$$ with all finite objects and morphisms restricted to $R$ as in the statement.

source.place: Second paragraph, final sentences: comparisons defined by their counits identify the specified natural maps; expanded restriction-form calculation.

proof.text: Apply derived point sections followed by constant-$R$ restriction to the equality in step 2. These are functors, so preserve its composites. Composing the resulting equality on the left with $\iota_n$ and substituting step 4 gives $$e_n\circ\bar d_{m,n}=\iota_nR\Gamma(s,\varepsilon_n)R\Gamma(s,d_{m,n})=\iota_nR\Gamma(s,v_{m,n})R\Gamma(s,\varepsilon_m)=q_{m,n}[0]\circ e_m.$$ This is an equality in $D(R)$ itself.

proof.text: For successive levels $r\ge m\ge n$, suppress only the canonical iterated-tensor associators. Work first on the ordinary etale realizations and then transport by [lem-coef-finite-dualizing]. The finite-Tor constructibility of every $\omega_j$ is supplied by [lem-coef-dualizing-construction]; the isomorphism $T_X^{r,m}\omega_r\cong\omega_m$ in [lem-coef-finite-dualizing] verifies the finite-Tor input hypothesis for each coefficient comparison below. Naturality and successive-reduction compatibility of $c$ in [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change], and the cocycle for $u$ in [lem-coef-finite-dualizing], give $$\begin{aligned}b_{r,n}&=F_n(u_{m,n}\circ T_X^{m,n}u_{r,m})\circ c_{r,n}\\&=F_n(u_{m,n})\circ F_n(T_X^{m,n}u_{r,m})\circ c^{m,n}_{T_X^{r,m}\omega_r}\circ T_s^{m,n}(c_{r,m})\\&=b_{m,n}\circ T_s^{m,n}(b_{r,m}).\end{aligned}$$ In the last equality use $F_n(T_X^{m,n}u_{r,m})\circ c^{m,n}_{T_X^{r,m}\omega_r}=c^{m,n}_{\omega_m}\circ T_s^{m,n}(F_m u_{r,m})$. Taking transposes under the composite tensor-restriction adjunction of [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower] yields $d_{r,n}=\operatorname{Res}_{r,m}(d_{m,n})\circ d_{r,m}$: this is the ordinary composition rule for transposes $h\mapsto\operatorname{Res}(h)\circ\eta$, obtained by substituting this formula twice and using unit naturality. The identity normalizations of $u$ and $c$ likewise give $d_{n,n}=1$. Step 4 identifies every $v$ with the quotient sheaf map, whose identity and composite are $q_{n,n}=1$ and $q_{r,n}=q_{m,n}q_{r,m}$. Applying the same sections functor gives all identity and composition assertions at section level. Every construction used above is finite; no representative of a strict dualizing tower or test object was selected.
